Appearance:
 Shri Vishal Patidar - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Saranjit Singh Chawla - Advocate for the responden
 Order

01. This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act is preferred challenging the award dated 01.03.2018 in Claim Case No.151 of 2016 passed by First Additional Member, MACT, Ratlam for enhancement of Rupees One lac compensation.
02. Liability is not disputed so only necessary facts are being discussed.
For injuries in Motor Vehicle Accident dated 04.01.2016 a total claim of Rs. 38,500/- has been awarded.
Rs. 19,103/- has been awarded in the head of medical expenses, Rs. 5000/- has been awarded in the head of transportation expenses and Rs. 5000/- in the head of attendant expenses.
Rupees 9,110/- towards damages caused to his motorcycle.

03. The appeal has been preferred on the ground that the appellant was taken to Government Hospital, Jawra and thereafter Geetanjali Hospital, Udaipur, Rajasthan and the injury was occurred on the head so the award is on lower side.
04. Counsel for the respondent Insurance Company opposed the prayer submitting that all the heads have been adequately compensated .
Perused the record.

06. After primary treatment at Jawra, Ratlam, the appellant was referred to Geetanjali Medical College and Hospital, Udaipur, Rajasthan, whereas he was admitted from 04.062016 to 06.06.2016 and vide Exhibits-P-42 to P-44 he was treated in follow up on 15.06.2016 and 27.07.2016.

entities.text: Geetanjali Medical College and Hospital, Udaipur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Medicines Epsolin-100 and capsule NUH EWZ were also recommended for further treatment.

The injury that was treated at Geetanjali Medical Hospital is on the scalp which necessitated the switchers, though the final report was submitted under Section 279, 337 and 338 of the IPC, but grievous injury could not be proved on record.

1 7.

Considering the duration of treatment an amount of Rs. 15,000/- is awarded in loss of earning during treatment, Rs.5000/- is further enhanced in the head of transportation and Rs. 5000/- is enhanced in the head of attendant expenses and Rs.10,000/- is enhanced in the head of pain and suffering.
A total sum of Rs. 35, 000/- is further enhanced.

8. With the aforesaid, this misc. appeal is partly allowed and total compensation of Rs.35,000/- is further enhanced with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of application ie 21.11.2016.
The enhanced amount be satisfied and distributed as per para 18 of the award of Tribunal.
9. Accordingly, this misc appeal is disposed of.
Pending I.As if any, shall stand closed.
